newsitem.title: JAPAN: UN says 60-65 pct of N.Korea children malnourished.
newsitem.headline: UN says 60-65 pct of N.Korea children malnourished.

text.p: United Nations Undersecretary General Yasushi Akashi, on a visit to North Korea, said 60 to 65 percent of children in flood-hit areas are suffering from malnutrition, the North Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said on Friday.
In a report monitored in Tokyo, KCNA said Akashi made the remarks on Thursday after visiting flood-hit areas in Huichon, Jagang Province, and Kujang and Pakchon, both in North Phyongan Province.
Akashi was quoted as saying he had witnessed serious food shortages in North Korea owing to the flood damage, and more food aid should be given.

Akashi, who heads the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs and is its emergency relief coordinator, arrived in Pyongyang on Tuesday on a five-day visit at the invitation of North Korea, which has been hit by famine following poor harvests due to the massive flooding in 1995 and 1996.
He is the first high-ranking U.N. official to visit North Korea to investigate the food crisis since mid-March, when a mission was sent by the World Food Program.
After his trip to North Korea, Akashi is scheduled to go to Seoul for talks with South Korean government officials. He is then due to stop in Tokyo.
